findings.title: Force execution paths are not fully specified
findings.description:
The design defines per-agent and bulk force protocols, says tick prefers bulk implementations, and requires tests exercising both paths (line 248). However, `tick()` accepts only `list[BulkForce]`, with no adapter or selection mechanism for per-agent forces.

Define how reference forces enter the pipeline without introducing per-agent execution into the vectorized hot path. A simple explicit reference adapter would satisfy the testing requirement without implicit dispatch.

findings.title: Neighbor contracts leave subset mapping and deterministic replacement ambiguous
findings.description:
`BulkForce` receives `neighbor_lists` and `active_indices`, but the design does not specify whether neighbor lists are population-indexed or active-subset-indexed. The spatial protocol also leaves self-inclusion and result ordering undefined.

These details matter to subsequent behavioral forces and slice 105’s requirement that replacing the spatial implementation preserve identical behavioral output. Specify list indexing, self-neighbor handling, and deterministic ordering or normalization so force implementations do not depend on undocumented brute-force behavior.

findings.title: Preserve the parent’s full-fidelity scale target
findings.description:
The parent architecture’s “Efficient large-scale evaluation” goal specifies **tens of thousands of agents at full behavioral fidelity on a single CPU process**. This slice touches the relevant state, force, and spatial interfaces but restates only vectorization requirements; its spatial discussion targets hundreds of agents.

Restate the architectural target and distinguish it from this slice’s deliberately limited brute-force baseline. Keep spatial optimization in slice 105, while making clear that the foundation’s interfaces must support the eventual target.
